criteria_results.criterion: Persist metrics.json with exact totals, district comparisons, and the reproducible calculation method for the supplied CSV. Use the exact keys row_count, scheduled_hours, completed_hours, incidents, completion_percent (2 decimal places), and districts. districts must be a JSON object keyed by district name. Every count, hour total and percentage in metrics.json must be a JSON number, never a string; format percentages to two decimal places in dashboard.html.
criteria_results.notes: metrics.json is persisted with exactly the required keys and numeric types. Recomputed independently from the supplied CSV: 6 rows; scheduled 12+8+10+14+6+9=59; completed 11+8+7+13+5+9=53; incidents 2+1+3+0+2+1=9; 53/59=89.8305 -> 89.83. Districts keyed North/South/West with totals 22/18/5 (81.82%), 14/13/3 (92.86%), 23/22/1 (95.65%); group sums reconcile exactly to the global totals (2+2+2=6, 22+14+23=59, 18+13+22=53, 5+3+1=9). All values are JSON numbers, none quoted. The reproducible method is embedded (input path, input sha256, encoding, parsing rule, per-metric formula, grouping rule, ROUND_HALF_UP rounding rule, three-way cross-check record). dashboard.html renders every percentage at two decimals: 89.83%, 81.82%, 92.86%, 95.65%.

criteria_results.criterion: Create a polished, self-contained dashboard.html that visibly presents every metric and requires no external assets.
criteria_results.notes: dashboard.html (11123 bytes) contains no http(s) references, no <script>, no <link rel=stylesheet>, no src= attributes, no @import and no url() — all visuals are pure CSS. It visibly presents all five top-level metrics (6 shifts, 59 h, 53 h, 9 incidents, 89.83% with progress track) plus a district comparison table with per-district shifts, scheduled hours, completed hours, incidents and completion percentage, a reconciliation footnote, and an all-districts total row. Layout is a deliberate dark navy theme with KPI cards, accent styling, inline bars and tabular numerals.

criteria_results.criterion: Use the approved render_dashboard capability to render dashboard.html in Chromium and save dashboard.png at exactly 1280x720, with legible content and no browser error page.
criteria_results.notes: dashboard.png exists (133960 bytes, sha256 ad132c2c…d3016c). Byte-level verification of IHDR gives width 1280, height 720, bit depth 8, color type 2, non-interlaced, confirmed independently by file(1); magic 89504e470d0a1a0a, valid chunk CRCs, IEND present, inflated IDAT exactly 720×3841 bytes. The render was performed through the approved local procedure mapped to render_dashboard (browser-screenshot.cjs, sha256 efc3bcb5…, exit 0, success:true, correct page title, empty stderr). Content is real and legible: 6038 distinct colours, mean luma 34.42, 28911 bright pixels (3.137%) in 11 structured horizontal bands spanning y=28..677 and x=31..1246, zero bright pixels in any 8px edge strip, 0% near-black — inconsistent with a Chromium error page. Output is byte-identical across three renders.

defects.issue: .probe-rerender.png is byte-identical to capability-probe.png (same sha256 35dc21b9…, same 40505 bytes) and is a duplicate scratch file, slightly against the specification's instruction to keep the artifact set concise apart from bounded capability-probe evidence.

In dashboard.html the header stamp reads 'metrics.json · sha256 502022dd…', but 502022dd… is the sha256 of input/rescue-shifts.csv; metrics.json's actual hash is c86780cc…. A cosmetic provenance mislabel that does not affect any computed value.

recommendations: Remove the redundant .probe-rerender.png probe duplicate to keep the delivered artifact set tight.
Relabel the dashboard header stamp to either cite the true metrics.json hash (c86780cc…) or explicitly label the cited hash as the input CSV.
review.verdict: PASS: PASS: All three acceptance criteria are satisfied from the artifact bytes. metrics.json carries the exact required keys with numeric typing and independently re-derivable values that match the CSV to the last decimal, plus a full reproducible method; dashboard.html is self-contained with no external assets and presents every global and per-district metric at two decimal places; dashboard.png was produced through the approved render path and is a valid 1280x720 PNG with legible, unclipped, reproducible rendered content and no error page. Only two cosmetic/minor hygiene issues remain.
